sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Quebec, Canada (Province of Quebec, target wrapper jurisdiction for the Canadian Business Corporation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Common Law for federal public and regulatory law and federal corporations; Quebec private law and provincial commercial company legislation rooted in Civil Law (Quebec Civil Code jurisprudence and French legal tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion, in force 29 December 1987
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 30 December 2018

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), RLRQ c. S-31.1, particularly ss. 5, 31, 51, 126 and related regulations respecting incorporation and internal governance
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) – Registraire central
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed in French or English via the CLIPIR online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the QBCA. Shares may be issued for no par value and for such consideration as the board determines. If the company accepts paid-in capital, the funds must be held in a Quebec-regulated banking institution and disbursed only for lawful business purposes, subject to anti-money laundering verification and board authorization.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: CERTIFIED FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CORPORATION NAME]: SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the corporation accepts the subscription for 1,000 common shares at a fair value of CAD 0.01 per share from the initial shareholder, payment of CAD 10.00 is acknowledged and directed to be deposited in the corporate bank account. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office in the Province of Quebec is established at [address] as per the Articles of Incorporation and until changed by the board. OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed President and Director, [Name] is appointed Secretary and Treasurer, and each officer is authorized to execute all necessary banking filings and routine contracts. The acts of these officers are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Quebec Enterprise Registrar / Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search through the Registraire's website or a licensed agent. If the desired name is distinctive, submit a name reservation request (Demande de réservation de nom) online. Ensure the name complies with the QBCA rules on legal singularity and prohibition of misleading names.
required_dossiers: Certificate of due diligence for proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, review refusal reasons, file an amendment to the reserved name, or provide justification for distinctiveness. Re-file within 30 days without losing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Quebec Enterprise Registrar / Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation (including registered office, director names, share structure and restrictions) and file electronically through the CLIPIR portal. Authority for incorporation is granted immediately upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation (attestation).
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation in French or English
Consent of directors (form from the Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, respond to the Registraire's notice within 15 days. Correct any formal defects in the articles or director names and re-submit without additional fees if within the initial filing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of initial bylaws and board governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Shareholders of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator shall adopt the initial bylaws (règlements) consistent with the QBCA. The first board meeting (or written resolution) appoints officers and authorizes share issuance. Minutes must be recorded and filed in the corporation's records book. A Declaration of Registered Office must be filed with the Registraire if not included in the articles.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or written resolution in lieu of meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For defective consent or procedural errors, convene a new meeting or circular resolution ratifying the prior informal actions. Update the register and keep original records for civil inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal tax and payroll registration (CRA + Revenu Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Business Number (BN) via CRA's online portal (or by fax/phone) and obtain a Goods & Services Tax (GST) account. For provincial compliance, register with Revenu Québec for QST (Quebec Sales Tax) and an employer number. Establish payroll accounts if employees are expected. Open a corporate bank account and register for payroll source deductions.
required_dossiers: Director and beneficial shareholder identification (passport, driver's license)
Banking account agreement and initial deposit confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account application is rejected, correct the identification details, ensure the registration is linked to the correct business number, and re-submit. For bank account issues, provide additional corporate documents (e.g., certificate of existence) and reconsider an alternative banking partner authorized in Canada.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – Financial Services Licensing Division, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance of Quebec
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Money Services Business (MSB) License – Category: Virtual Card and Payment Services (limited to corporate expense cards) under the Act respecting money-services businesses (ARMSB) and the Business Companies Act licensing regime

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Environmental Impact Assessment Registration (exempt from full study for non-industrial office-based commercial activity; a preliminary declaration and follow-up registration may still be required if the company operates a data center or server farm in a sensitive zone)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office and IT operations, no significant discharge to water or uncontrolled volatile organic compounds (VOCs) expected. Any backup generator must meet Quebec's Clean Air Regulation (RA Ch. Q-2, r. 4.1) and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act (VOC limits from electronics and cleaning agents ≤ 200 ppb; waste handling via RecycFluo for lamps, batteries and electronic waste). Wastewater discharge, if any, shall comply with municipal sewer by-laws and the Regulation respecting sewage systems (Q-2, r. 22).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a municipal fire safety permit (permis de sécurité incendie) for the registered office location, including fire extinguisher placement and emergency lighting inspection. Submit a structural load notification to the borough office if the floor area exceeds 300 m². Clearance is required from the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) confirming compliance with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (RLRQ, c. S-2.1), including ergonomic evaluation of workspaces, training of first responders, and a confined-space protocol if a server room is present.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax, with the 'My Business Account' portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial income tax, with the 'Cliquez Affaires' portal at https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident corporations must first obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA by filing Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Accounts', or by using Business Registration Online. After obtaining the BN, the corporation must add a GST/HST program account (RT) for the supply of taxable goods or services in Canada; if the corporation has no permanent establishment and all material decisions are made abroad, a non-resident agent may be required for service of documents. Separate registration is then required with Revenu Québec to obtain a QST identification number by filing the Quebec registration form through the Cliquez Affaires portal, providing the BN, legal name, address, business structure, and director or officer information. The same BN can be used for income tax, payroll, and GST/HST accounts, but the QST number remains a distinct Revenu Québec identifier. No minimum capital is required for the Business Corporation, and non-resident ownership is permitted subject to filing disclosure requirements for foreign ownership and any applicable sectoral licences.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election; entity classification is determined under the Income Tax Act and established Canadian common-law principles. A Canadian Business Corporation is automatically treated as an entity-level taxpayer subject to income tax on its worldwide revenue. Available elections relevant to cross-border fintech operations include the section 85(1) rollover election, the section 216 non-resident net-income election, the section 249.1 election to use a non-calendar fiscal period for tax purposes, and, in the context of hybrid mismatch rules, sections 18.2 to 18.4 apply automatically without any elective safe harbour. For GST/QST purposes, a registrant may elect to use the Quick Method or annual filing where legislation provides, though financial institutions do not qualify; no election changes the fundamental entity-level taxation of the corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% federally; Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% provincially, for a combined headline rate of 14.975% on taxable goods and services in Quebec. Financial services are generally exempt from GST and QST, but supplies of financial services to non-residents may be zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act and the QST Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (exclusive of exempt financial services and supplies made through a permanent establishment) in the current calendar quarter together with the preceding three consecutive calendar quarters triggers mandatory GST/HST registration. For QST purposes, Revenu Québec applies an analogous CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, calculated on the supplier's worldwide taxable supplies, at which mandatory QST registration becomes effective in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national or Quebec real-time fiscal clearance, government API stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate applies as of the current filing year. Electronic invoicing is accepted and encouraged by the CRA and Revenu Québec, but there is no statutory requirement for preclearance or digital stamping of B2B invoices. All registered corporate-card issuers must retain complete invoice images, transaction-level interchange and settlement records, bank confirmation files, and underlying contract documentation to substantiate GST/QST treatment upon review. A transition toward mandatory e-invoicing is under active policy discussion in Quebec, but no mandatory clearance mandate is currently in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Excise Tax Act for a supply of financial services made to a non-resident person who is not registered under the GST/HST and does not have a significant presence or carrying-on-business nexus in Canada. A corporate virtual-card issuer must demonstrate that the card issuing, spend-management, and processing services are acquired by the non-resident client for use predominantly outside Canada, and that the recipient is the true legal counter-party. For tangible goods exported from Canada, zero-rating applies if the goods are delivered by the supplier to a common carrier or by another qualifying export mechanism via the Canada Border Services Agency export declaration and the supplier has timely evidence of export. Quebec QST zero-rating generally mirrors the federal GST financial-services export rules for supplies made to non-residents and supplies shipped or delivered outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Completed Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A or the electronic CAED version) filed with the Canada Border Services Agency
Transport document evidencing physical export, such as a Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, road manifest, or bare-carrier certificate
Commercial invoice and supply contract identifying the non-resident buyer, full goods/services description, and contract value

Bank outward/export payment evidence, including an Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT/telegraphic transfer confirmation, or a Canadian bank wire credit advice showing receipt of payment from the non-resident counter-party
Carrier or freight-forwarder certificate of export, where applicable, to supplement the customs declaration and transport documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated supplies within four years of the original return, and an unlimited review period applies where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. If export documentation is missing or inadequate, the entire zero-rating claim is clawed back, converting the supplies to taxable at the combined 14.975% rate plus interest. Negligent or deliberate overstating of zero-rated revenue triggers the Excise Tax Act gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the understated net tax, further section 285 penalties for false statements, potential criminal prosecution under section 327, and equivalent QST penalties under the QST Act. The taxpayer bears the burden of proving physical export and correct recipient status; internal card operations, interchange records, settlement audit trails, and FX repatriation evidence are therefore critical to preserve.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) as monetary authority; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/CFT regulator; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for federally regulated bank counterparties; Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) of Quebec as provincial securities and money-services-business regulator; Global Affairs Canada for sanctions administration under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the United Nations Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD). No exchange controls are in force; the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act authorize a free-floating exchange rate. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred cross-border without ministerial authorization or conversion mandate. Statutory frictions are limited to (i) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (default 25% on dividends, reduced by treaty), (ii) FINTRAC and Customs Act reporting of currency or monetary instruments equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 crossing the border, (iii) FATCA/CRS self-certification, and (iv) Investment Canada Act notification/review if the inbound capital injection constitutes a reviewable non-Canadian acquisition of a Quebec business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rules exist in Canada. The former Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951; there is no mandated timeline, minimum conversion ratio, or central bank deposit requirement for foreign currency receipts. Export settlements may be held in any convertible currency, subject only to standard accounting (IFRS), tax reporting, and OFAC/United Nations/Canadian sanctions screening obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec (Desjardins Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct equivalence. Canada does not recognize a European Economic Area EMI passport. A non-resident fintech/EMI must establish a Canadian presence: (i) register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); (ii) register as a money-services business with the AMF under Quebec's Act respecting money-services businesses (CQLR c S-41.1) when operating in Quebec; (iii) register as a payment service provider with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) where RPAA thresholds are met; and (iv) secure a principal-member sponsorship from an OSFI-regulated Canadian bank for Visa/Mastercard program access, as direct network membership is not available to non-deposit-taking fintechs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permissible. FINTRAC and OSFI permit virtual KYC/identity verification provided the financial institution applies enhanced due diligence, including government-issued photo ID validation, corporate registry cross-checks (Registraire des entreprises du Québec), beneficial-ownership attestations, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth documentation. No statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically; however, certain banks' internal risk committees may require a live video interview with senior management and, in high-risk scenarios (card issuing for cross-border B2B spend), an in-person visit by the bank's commercial account manager in Montreal or Toronto. Quebec civil-law notarization of board resolutions and director consents may be required for the account signatory schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification: unauthorized card issuance without a Canadian banking licence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB registration certificate; AMF money-services-business licence or exemption letter; sponsor bank program-management agreement; board-approved AML/CFT compliance program under PCMLTFA with designated Compliance Officer; OSFI neutrality letter confirming non-deposit-taking status under Bank Act s. 545.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transaction volume and velocity red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual transaction volume and value projections; FINTRAC risk-based assessment report; real-time transaction monitoring architecture; correspondent banking counterparty list (restricted to OSFI/Schedule I banks); Mastercard and Visa network participation certificates; sanctions screening procedure covering Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and OFAC SDN list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sponsorship dependency and third-party risk management gap
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Program management agreement evidencing sponsor oversight; audit and data-residency architecture; Quebec Law 25 (Loi 25) privacy compliance register; transaction-level audit trail maps; outsourcing framework satisfying FINTRAC record-keeping and OSFI operational risk guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual card product ambiguity as a substitute for consumer credit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate-only eligibility criteria and KYB policy; NAICS 522320 / ISIC 6619 business-purpose declarations; employer-employee expense management workflows; contractual prohibition of consumer and personal use; restricted merchant-category code (MCC) policy; negative list of prohibited high-risk verticals (gambling, digital assets, firearms).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Conversion of collected cardholder funds to stored value without deposit-taking authority
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Non-deposit-taking legal opinion; sponsor bank segregated reserve account agreement; independent third-party audit of safeguarded funds; settlement reconciliation policy; Quebec Consumer Protection Act inapplicability analysis for pure B2B corporate cards.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended routing: SWIFT MT103 wire from the foreign parent/investor to the Quebec corporation's CAD clearing account held at an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank. Instruct the remitter to use purpose code 5110 (capital contribution and similar transactions) or 5210 (investment in the reporting economy) in the MT103 field 72/77B, with clear narrative: 'Non-resident equity injection for treasury and virtual card program operations'. Verification package: shareholder resolution authorizing subscription, share-transfer ledger, source-of-funds evidence (audited financial statements or bank statements of the parent), Canadian counsel legal opinion on no Investment Canada Act review (or notification confirmation), FATCA/CRS self-certification (W-8BEN-E or CDS1), and sanctions-clearance screening through FINTRAC and Global Affairs Canada lists. For domestic CAD transfers subsequent to the initial injection, use the Lynx high-value payment system (Payments Canada ISO 20022) directly via the clearing bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements performed via SWIFT MT103 (covered/uncovered) with full correspondent chain transparency; commercial letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700 by the sponsor bank for large-value procurement and non-card vendor disbursements when LC security is contractually required; FX trades settled via CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) where the counterparty dealer is a CLS settlement member; domestic and cross-border card settlement aggregated through VisaNet (Visa Direct) or the Mastercard central clearing and settlement system, with daily net settlement executed in CAD across the sponsor bank's settlement account; CAD domestic vendor payouts cleared via Lynx or Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) wires and EFT per Payments Canada rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable forward contracts (plain-vanilla FX forwards) executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a master FX forward agreement with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank or registered Ontario/Quebec derivatives dealer
CAD/EUR deliverable forward contracts for European cross-border treasury concentration purposes
FX swaps (cross-currency swaps) bridging settlement currencies between the USD Visa/Mastercard settlement leg and the CAD treasury leg, collateralized under a Credit Support Annex

European-style plain-vanilla FX options (OTC) for premium-free and limited-cost hedging, permissible under OSFI derivative margin rules and AMF derivatives registration requirements when marketed in Quebec

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are practically unavailable for CAD OTC markets due to full CAD convertibility; if a counterparty proposes NDF hedging against CAD, the transaction should be rejected for lack of economic substance and replaced with deliverable forwards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration Annuelle) — Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule — file during the month of the enterprise's registration anniversary; the REQ annual reminder specifies the exact due period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional fee plus interest under the fee regulation; repeated non-filing allows the Registraire to cancel the enterprise registration and ultimately effect administrative dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (including Individuals with Significant Control return, where applicable) — Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule — within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Director may send a notice of intention to dissolve after consecutive annual-return defaults; dissolution becomes effective 120 days after service unless the corporation files, corrects, or is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-period rule — no later than six months after the end of each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, with a separate repeated-failure penalty; interest accrues on outstanding amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-period rule — within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty plus interest under the Québec Taxation Act; repeated non-filing may result in loss of certain deductions and increased director exposure for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Money Services Business (MSB) Registration Renewal and Annual AML/ATF Compliance Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); additional licence oversight by Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) where applicable in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: MSB registration is valid for a two-year cycle; renewal must be filed before expiry. Annual AML policy, risk assessment, and compliance-program updating align with the enterprise's fiscal-year cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a current MSB registration is an offence; FINTRAC may impose administrative monetary penalties and the Quebec AMF may suspend or revoke licences, prohibiting continued card-issuing activity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for a public or offering corporation, a licensed money-services business or payment-service provider whose regulator requires reviewed audited financial statements, and any corporation whose shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand an audit. A private CBCA/QBCA corporation may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian ASPE under the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is required for public reporting issuers and is generally prescribed for regulated fintech/financial-license statutory reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Quebec annual declaration must confirm directors, registered office, and individuals with control holding 25% or more of the corporation's voting rights or market value. Any beneficial-ownership or director change in the year must be reflected in the REQ update within the prescribed filing period and in the CBCA individuals-with-significant-control register; no separate confirmation is required when there is no such change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per year for registered office/registered agent services in Quebec (federal and provincial annual returns are typically an additional professional fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,000 for a small-to-mid-size virtual-card issuing fintech or money-services corporation; a scoped regulatory audit typically starts at approximately USD 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate income tax rate of 15% plus Quebec general corporate income tax rate of 11.5%, producing a combined statutory headline rate of 26.5%; reduced rates apply to the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income for a Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Quebec applies a reduced small-business rate of 3.2% on the same income base; SR&ED tax credits, Quebec innovation incentives, and the Patent Box regime may further reduce the effective rate. No general statutory tax holiday exists for virtual-card issuers in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed through CRA EFILE/XML electronic filing portal (mandatory for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; balance-due tax instalments are payable quarterly for ordinary CCPCs and monthly for large corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due tax is payable within 2 months after fiscal year-end, or 3 months for a CCPC eligible for the Small Business Deduction in the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, fiscal period end, corporate type (CCPC/non-CCPC), registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify whether the corporation is foreign-controlled; disclose beneficial ownership and country of control; confirm status as a Canadian resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income or loss from T2 schedules, including virtual card interchange income, sponsorship fees, platform charges, and digital expense-management revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report entire Canadian-source business income; intercompany transactions with non-resident parents or affiliates must be supported by arm's-length transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before and after loss carry-forwards, and base amount for federal rate calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty deductions affecting taxable income are applied only where the relevant Canada DTA is explicitly incorporated; otherwise domestic law governs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base federal corporate income tax payable and federal tax abatement/indicator for provincial allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec corporate tax liability is computed separately on CO-17; the federal abatement only reduces federal tax, not Quebec tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of reportable transactions with non-resident non-arm's-length persons, using the CAD 1,000,000 aggregate transaction threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File T106 for all payments to related foreign entities, IP licensing arrangements, software service fees, and card network procurement fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months; late instalment interest charged at prescribed rates; repeated electronic filing violations may attract additional administrative penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed through Revenu Québec's clicSÉF or authorized internet transmission portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly instalments for Quebec income tax and employer source-deduction remittances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed within 6 months of fiscal year-end; final Quebec tax payment is due within 2 months after fiscal year-end, or 3 months for a CCPC entitled to the reduced Quebec small-business rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), legal name, mailing address, date of incorporation, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Extra-provincial corporations carrying on business in Quebec must be registered; provide a known agent for service if the registered office is outside Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, fees, interchange income, card programme management income, interest from payment float, and other revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income between Quebec and other jurisdictions using the prescribed Quebec allocation formula only if a permanent establishment exists in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after adjustments for Quebec Taxation Act additions, deductions, and loss carry-overs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-exchange gains or losses associated with cross-border card settlement must be included; losses claimed must meet the Quebec continuity-of-business rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporate income tax payable before and after non-refundable tax credits, including digitalisation and innovation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: DTA relief does not reduce Quebec provincial income tax; reduced treaty rates affect only federal Part XIII withholding, not Quebec CO-17 liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec levies a late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month, up to 12 months; late-payment interest and administrative monetary penalties apply for missing information returns; directors may be liable for source deductions and QST not remitted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; Quebec imposes no additional provincial dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payer must obtain a declaration or Form NR301 from the non-resident beneficial owner before remitting at a reduced DTA rate; a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the relevant treaty jurisdiction must be produced on CRA request; if excess was withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund by filing Form NR7 or an amended Part XIII return. Revenu Québec does not maintain a separate treaty-relief mechanism for federal DTA reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding tax is 25% on interest and 25% on IP royalties paid to non-residents; statutory exemption applies to many arm's-length interest payments not in the nature of participating debt. DTA rates commonly reduce interest to 0% and IP royalties to between 0% and 10%, contingent on beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate non-resident non-arm's-length transaction value triggers T106 filing and mandatory contemporaneous Local File/TP documentation; CAD 750,000,000 consolidated MNE group revenue triggers Country-by-Country (CbC) report and corresponding Master File support.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations exist in Canada; the doctrine is effectuated through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA section 245), Quebec Taxation Act section 1078.2, and the 'economic substance' jurisprudence requiring a genuine commercial purpose. A virtual-card issuer or holding company lacking real operations, employees, or substantive business purpose is a high-priority audit target.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Wilful Failure to File
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing virtual-card interchange revenue, processing fees, or sponsor programme income; issuing false invoices; using undisclosed foreign bank accounts; or fabricating expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239: fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, or both; plus civil interest and gross-negligence penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorised evasion may be personally assessed for unremitted source deductions under section 227.1; the corporate veil is pierced for fraud; travel restrictions and passport surrender may be imposed pending criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recklessly filing incomplete T2 or CO-17 returns, failing to report reportable transactions, or participating in a silent shell-entity arrangement to obstruct CRA/Revenu Québec audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 163(2): 50% gross-negligence penalty on the understated tax; Quebec Taxation Act imposes an analogous 50% penalty, plus interest and attributable costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for corporate GST/QST and payroll remittances if they knowingly participated in failure to remit; civil restitution may extend to monies diverted through shell companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, or card-network service fees at non-commercial rates; failing to prepare or file T106 Information Returns for CAD 1,000,000+ cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 247(2) permits CRA to recharacterise and adjust cross-border transactions to the arm's-length price; section 247(3) imposes a penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment where documentation is deficient; no cap applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for TP adjustments but become personally liable for associated withheld amounts if they knowingly authorised the mispricing or hid documentation from CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards without FINTRAC money-services-business registration or required Quebec payment-services licensing; accepting anonymous reloads from shell entities; failing to maintain AML/KYC records for virtual-card clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation; criminal conviction may lead to fines up to CAD 2,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec Autorité des marchés financiers may impose additional sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers can be personally named in FINTRAC AMPs and criminal proceedings; travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment apply upon indictment; corporate veil protection is unavailable where the corporation was a deliberate sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / No Economic Substance / Abusive Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec holding corporation with no physical office, no employees, and no genuine commercial activity as a conduit to park foreign card revenues, claim small-business deductions, or avoid Part XIII dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply GAAR to deny the tax benefit and recharacterise the conduit arrangement; false or sham documentation triggers section 239 evasion penalties and gross-negligence penalties under section 163; interest compounds from the original filing date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the corporation's unremitted withholdings and GST/QST; fraudulent conveyance doctrine permits piercing the veil; criminal conviction may impose imprisonment and travel bans.
